## How it works

- [statement] Amantadine is a weak uncompetitive NMDA-receptor antagonist; the Gocovri label states that its therapeutic mechanism is unknown and distinguishes anticholinergic-like adverse effects from demonstrated direct anticholinergic activity. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label warns against abrupt withdrawal because of worsening parkinsonism and neuropsychiatric symptoms; for treatment longer than 4 weeks it advises, if possible, halving the dose for the final week. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The 2003 Cochrane amantadine review found insufficient evidence for efficacy and safety for general idiopathic Parkinson symptoms from older trials; its searches extended through 2001, so that conclusion does not include the 2017 EASE LID dyskinesia trial. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8715353/ · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5710325/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label starts treatment at 137 mg at bedtime and increases after one week to 274 mg at bedtime; it explicitly states that Gocovri is not substitutable with other immediate-release or extended-release amantadine products. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] EASE LID excluded patients with MMSE scores below 24, estimated glomerular filtration rates below 50 mL/min/1.73 m2, and prior amantadine intolerance or lack of response; these exclusions limit direct generalization to such patients. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5710325/ · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] Gocovri renal dosing is formulation-specific: the February 2026 label recommends 68.5 mg initially and a maximum of 137 mg daily for moderate impairment, 68.5 mg daily for severe impairment, and contraindicates use in end-stage renal disease below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] NICE recommendations tagged 2017 advise against vitamin E as neuroprotective treatment, restrict co-enzyme Q10 neuroprotective use to clinical trials, and advise against creatine supplements in Parkinson disease; these adjunct supplements should not be presented as established neuroprotective therapy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2017-07-19) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 2017 EASE LID trial, the week 12 placebo-adjusted improvement in Unified Dyskinesia Rating Scale score was 7.9 points. This is evidence for the studied extended-release product and population, rather than proof that every amantadine formulation is equivalent. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5710325/ · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label indicates this extended-release amantadine product for dyskinesia during levodopa-based treatment and as adjunctive treatment for off episodes; these are product-specific indications. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] Hallucinations, peripheral edema and dizziness were prominent adverse events in EASE LID; Gocovri prescribing information also lists these adverse reactions. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5710325/ · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf
- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label warns that concomitant drugs with anticholinergic properties may potentiate anticholinergic-like adverse effects; it advises reducing the anticholinergic drug or Gocovri dose if atropine-like effects appear. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] Benztropine and trihexyphenidyl are anticholinergic options used particularly in younger patients; cognitive impairment, confusion, hallucinations, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and urinary retention restrict their usefulness, especially with advancing age. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/anticholinergic-drugs · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8728160/
- [statement] The Parkinson Foundation describes anticholinergics as predominantly useful for tremor with little effect on other symptoms; the Cochrane review found motor benefit over placebo but conflicting results and insufficient support for a preferential effect on tremor. The latter limits claims of established symptom selectivity. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/anticholinergic-drugs · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8728160/

## Research summary — Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

Amantadine has formulation-specific evidence for dyskinesia, while its precise therapeutic mechanism remains unknown. Extended-release Gocovri requires attention to renal function, hallucinations, edema and withdrawal. Anticholinergics such as benztropine and trihexyphenidyl have a restricted role because cognitive and peripheral adverse effects can outweigh motor benefit, especially in older people. Clinical emphasis on tremor should be distinguished from the weak trial evidence for preferential tremor efficacy. Older inconclusive amantadine reviews address different evidence from later formulation-specific trials. NICE discourages several proposed neuroprotective supplements.

## Source disagreement — Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

The Parkinson Foundation describes anticholinergics as predominantly useful for tremor with little effect on other symptoms; the Cochrane review found motor benefit over placebo but conflicting results and insufficient support for a preferential effect on tremor. The latter limits claims of established symptom selectivity.
